power.title: Horsepower, old and new
power.sub: Toyota's figures. The hybrid number is combined system output.

torque.title: Peak torque, old and new
torque.sub: Pound-feet, as advertised. The hybrid makes its peak at 2,400 rpm, against 3,600 rpm for the V8.

cargo.title: Cargo space, old and new
cargo.sub: Cubic feet, as published. The new Sequoia's third row slides, so its space behind the third row runs from 11.5 cu ft (slid back) to 22.3 (slid forward).
cargo.source: Toyota, via Hooniverse and The Drive

tow.title: How much it can tow
tow.sub: Toyota's maximum towing ratings, in kilograms, with pounds in parentheses. Both peaks are for 2-wheel-drive versions.

mpg.title: Fuel economy, 4x4
mpg.sub: EPA combined miles per gallon for 4x4 versions. 2-wheel-drive versions are rated at 15 mpg (V8) and 22 mpg (hybrid).

fuelcost.title: A year of fuel
fuelcost.sub: 15,000 miles at $4 a gallon, using the 4x4 EPA combined figures above: 14 and 20 mpg. An example, not a forecast.

ch1-hero.want: A 2017–2022 Sequoia, ideally a TRD Pro or Limited

ch2-hero.want: A 2023–2026 Sequoia driving, ideally a Platinum, 1794 Edition or Capstone

ch3-hero.want: The Sequoia's third row or cargo area, ideally showing the sliding third row or cargo shelf
ch3-hero.alt: The cargo area of a Toyota Sequoia

ch4-hero.want: A Sequoia TRD Pro off-road, or a Sequoia towing

ch5-hero.want: A Sequoia on a family trip, or its underside

ch6-hero.want: An old and a new Sequoia together, or a 2023–2026 Sequoia outside
